question: Should OpenClaw accept a core node-to-model tool advertisement contract, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90431 be the implementation path after conflict and review-blocker resolution?
rationale: This changes the trust boundary by letting connected nodes influence model-visible tools and route execution through node.invoke, which automation cannot accept without maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Accept the PR 90431 direction after repairs
options.body: Use the existing candidate path, but require conflict resolution, API compatibility cleanup, and explicit trust/provenance acceptance before merge.

options.title: Redesign the node tool contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the design owner and ask for a narrower successor that changes protocol, inventory, and policy semantics differently.

options.title: Keep plugin wrappers as the only supported route
options.body: Reject direct node-advertised tools for now and require integrations to use existing plugin plus node.invoke patterns.

recommendation.title: Accept the PR 90431 direction after repairs
recommendation.body: Use the existing candidate path, but require conflict resolution, API compatibility cleanup, and explicit trust/provenance acceptance before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the candidate implementation and is the clearest routing owner for the protocol/runtime/security decision surfaced by the issue.
